output: Hypothesis: The first principal component (PC1) of the forms of capital during the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) periods does not show a statistically significant difference, suggesting that the patterns of capital forms during these periods may be similar. The variables chosen for analysis were the PC1 values derived from the forms of capital (e.g., Hatchets and Swords, House Size, Copper and Gold, etc.). The relationship between the PC1 values of the two periods was analyzed using a t-test, which showed no statistically significant difference (p-value = 0.334).
